comments.text:
On August 26, 2026, an enormous rock-and-ice avalanche near the Langtang Lirung peak on the Nepal-Tibet border triggered the deadliest mountain collapse and flash flood the Himalayas have ever recorded. 

What Happened:
1) The Collapse: A massive section of bedrock and glacier at an altitude of about 5,200 meters detached cleanly, plunging roughly 1,200 meters to the valley floor. 
2) Seismic Shock: The descent was so violent that global seismometers initially registered it as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake caused by the impact. 
3) The Debris Flow: The falling rock, ice, and debris dammed the Lhende Khola (Lehende Cola) river before bursting into a catastrophic flood wave that surged nearly 100 km downstream along the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi corridors. 
4) Speed: The debris flow traveled the first 22 km in under 7 minutes, hitting speeds up to 193 km per hour. 

Devastation and Impact:
1) Casualties: Nearly 1,000 people lost their lives, and thousands more were reported missing across Nepal and Tibet, including foreign trekkers and tourists. 
2) Infrastructure: Dozens of bridges, schools, and hydropower projects were destroyed, wiping out major trade routes to China and knocking hundreds of megawatts offline from the national grid.
3) Displaced: Ten of thousands of residents were displaced, and entire low-lying settlements were completely swept away. 

The Cause:
1) Climate Factor: Scientists analyzing satellite and drone imagery determined that decades of rising regional temperatures thawed frozen internal permafrost, weakening the structural integrity of the mountain's bedrock and adhesive ice cracks.
2) Growing Threat: Experts warn that as the Hindu Kush Himalaya region..often called the "Third Pole", continues to heat up, destabilized slopes and melting glaciers present severe, recurring hazards for millions living downstream.

comments.author: @eddieleong6490
comments.text: The best narrative on the disaster so far.  Nepal suffered the most.  The best policy is to move all towns and villages off the deep valleys until China, and the world can agree to map the Himalayan valleys continuously and to provide early warnings via international agencies and not depend on China-Nepal signing agreements.  Typhoons, volcanic eruptions, even a flood of earthquakes do not require any one country to permit its disclosures. Deep valley rockfalls, floods, etc. can also be monitored in real time and warnings issued.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
